pages.scene: A weathered lighthouse stands on rocky cliffs against a sunset sky, with a young girl gazing up at it.

pages.text: The Lighthouse Keeper
Maya had always loved the old lighthouse, and she visited it every summer when she came to stay with her grandmother.
pages.scene: A girl with windblown hair stands before a tall white lighthouse, waves crashing on rocks below.

pages.text: "That lighthouse has been in our family for three generations," Grandma often said, her eyes sparkling with pride.
pages.scene: An elderly woman with kind eyes sits in a rocking chair, gesturing as she tells stories.

pages.text: This summer felt different, though, because Grandma seemed tired and the lighthouse needed more repairs than ever before.
pages.scene: Peeling paint on lighthouse walls, broken shutters, and an elderly woman looking concerned.

pages.text: "The light must never go out," Grandma whispered to Maya one evening, and Maya understood this was about more than electricity.
pages.scene: Grandmother and granddaughter watching the beacon spin as dusk falls over the ocean.

pages.text: Although Maya was only eleven, she decided she would help keep the lighthouse running while her grandmother rested.
pages.scene: Maya with a determined expression, rolling up her sleeves in front of maintenance supplies.

pages.text: "Are you sure you can handle this?" asked Mr. Chen, the harbor master, when he heard her plan.
pages.scene: A friendly middle-aged man in a captain's hat looks down at Maya with concern and curiosity.

pages.text: "I can learn," Maya replied firmly, and something in her voice made him believe her.
pages.scene: Maya standing tall, meeting the harbor master's gaze with confidence.

pages.text: Every morning before sunrise, Maya climbed the spiral staircase to check the great lens, and every evening she made sure the beacon was ready.
pages.scene: Maya ascending a narrow spiral staircase inside the lighthouse, light streaming through small windows.

pages.text: The work was harder than she expected, but she refused to complain because she knew how much it meant to her grandmother.
pages.scene: Maya wiping sweat from her brow while polishing the lighthouse lens.

pages.text: "You remind me of myself when I was young," Grandma murmured one afternoon, watching Maya work from her chair.
pages.scene: Grandmother smiling warmly at Maya through the lighthouse window.

pages.text: One night, a terrible storm rolled in from the sea, and the waves grew taller than Maya had ever seen them.
pages.scene: Dark storm clouds over churning seas, lightning in the distance, rain lashing the lighthouse.

pages.text: "The backup generator," Grandma called out weakly, "you must check the backup generator, or the light will fail!"
pages.scene: Grandmother struggling to rise from bed, reaching toward Maya with urgency.

pages.text: Maya raced down to the basement, and her heart pounded as she saw water seeping through the foundation.
pages.scene: Dark basement with water pooling on the floor, old machinery and a worried girl.

pages.text: Although she was terrified, she remembered everything her grandmother had taught her about the old generator.
pages.scene: Maya's hands working on machinery, her face lit by a flashlight beam.

pages.text: "Come on, come on," she muttered to herself, and then the engine roared back to life.
pages.scene: The generator humming with power, relief washing over Maya's face.

pages.text: When she climbed back up the stairs, she saw the beacon spinning brightly against the raging storm.
pages.scene: The lighthouse beam cutting through rain and darkness, ships visible in the distance.

pages.text: "You saved them," Mr. Chen said the next morning, gesturing toward three fishing boats in the harbor that had followed the light safely home.
pages.scene: Morning sun, fishing boats safely docked, grateful sailors waving at the lighthouse.

pages.text: Maya felt tears in her eyes, but she quickly wiped them away and smiled.
pages.scene: Maya with misty eyes and a proud smile, the harbor behind her.

pages.text: "I only did what any lighthouse keeper would do," she answered quietly.
pages.scene: Maya standing humbly, the lighthouse towering behind her.

pages.text: Grandma was waiting on the porch when Maya returned, and she opened her arms wide for a long embrace.
pages.scene: Grandmother and granddaughter hugging on a cottage porch, morning light around them.

pages.text: "I knew you could do it," Grandma said softly, and neither of them needed to say anything more.
pages.scene: Close-up of grandmother and Maya, faces full of love and understanding.

pages.text: From that day on, Maya spent every summer learning everything about the lighthouse, and she knew that someday it would be hers to protect.
pages.scene: Maya studying old logbooks and charts at a wooden desk in the lighthouse.

pages.text: Although she would grow up and see the world, this lighthouse on the rocky shore would always be her true home.
pages.scene: Older Maya standing beside her grandmother, both looking out at the sunset over the sea.

pages.text: The beacon continued to spin, night after night, guiding sailors safely through the darkness just as it had for generations before.
pages.scene: The lighthouse at night, its beam sweeping across calm waters, stars above.

pages.text: The End
pages.scene: The lighthouse silhouetted against a peaceful dawn sky.

story_bible.premise: An eleven-year-old girl proves herself ready to carry on her family's three-generation legacy as lighthouse keepers when she saves three fishing boats during a violent storm while her aging grandmother can only watch.

character_arcs.Maya: Loving granddaughter → Determined helper → Tested by storm → Proven keeper → Legacy bearer
character_arcs.Grandma: Proud keeper growing frail → Worried about the future → Trusting Maya → Passing the torch
character_arcs.Mr. Chen: Skeptical adult → Believes in Maya → Witnesses her triumph → Confirms her capability

story_bible.setting: A weathered lighthouse on a rocky coastline, summer season. The lighthouse is old but beloved, showing signs of age—peeling paint, broken shutters. Inside is warm and full of history. The sea is a constant presence, calm some days, terrifying during storms.
story_bible.plot_summary:
Maya visits her grandmother's lighthouse every summer, but this year something is different. Grandma is tired, the lighthouse needs repairs, and there's an unspoken weight to Grandma's words about the light never going out.

Though only eleven, Maya decides to take on the lighthouse keeper duties. Mr. Chen, the harbor master, is skeptical, but Maya's determination convinces him. She learns the routines—climbing the spiral stairs before dawn, checking the great lens, maintaining the equipment.

The true test comes when a terrible storm hits. Grandma is too weak to help, and the backup generator fails just as waves pound the foundation. Alone in the flooded basement, terrified but remembering her grandmother's teachings, Maya gets the generator running.

When the storm passes, Mr. Chen reveals that three fishing boats made it safely to harbor because of her light. Maya downplays her heroism, but Grandma knows the truth—the legacy has been passed. Maya will grow up and see the world, but this lighthouse will always be her home, and she will always be its keeper.

Worry - Grandma is aging, lighthouse deteriorating
Weight of legacy - "The light must never go out"

Struggle - The work is harder than expected
Crisis begins - Terrible storm rolls in
Terror - Alone in flooded basement, generator dead
Triumph - Generator roars back to life
Legacy secured - This will always be her home

story_bible.level_adaptation: Band D allows complex sentences, dialogue, and emotional nuance. Used compound and complex sentence structures throughout. Vocabulary includes challenging words (weathered, beacon, determination) while keeping core narrative accessible. Emotional complexity preserved through showing rather than telling.
story_bible.visual_style: Rich watercolor illustrations with dramatic lighting. The lighthouse is a character—shown in golden summer light, ominous storm gray, and triumphant beacon glow. Maya's expressions carry her emotional journey. Water and light are recurring visual motifs.
